notes.title: v1.11 (July 6)
notes.content:
v1.11! (6th July)
Basically "quality of life" changes, fixing some gameplay elements that were kind of annoying


 No more language selection screen on every startup (which was redundant), now when you confirm your language, it automatically gets saved (to change it again, reset your data)
 Audio restoration, updated all of the sound effects to be output as stereo (it sounds a bit better I think)
 Jumper: made this minigame less "boring" - now you can hold down shift/right click (B) to speed up the barrels and make them go much faster - saves you time and increases the fast-paced action!
 Recker: added a warning sign to indicate it even clearer that you shouldn't touch the construction workers or else game over
 Laser Launch: in the asteroid-destroy segment, you now have lives, it is more challenging to survive until the 2 minute mark, and you get more points for destroying larger asteroids
 Goofball Pinball: a subtle improvement with the physics of the ball
 Whack-A-Gopher: fixed an instance in which the game would crash when matching smarty gophers in the extra bonus "bootleg Candy Crush" segment...
 The Ball Pit Battle: updated the ballpit kid sprites (before it was inconsistent pixel-wise, they were 8-bit graphics in an 16-bit environment lol)
 Performance improvement, added some delta timing to various in-game elements, specifically with the in-game timer
 Fixed a bug where the game crashed when you very quickly switched back-and-forth between two filters

* Reminder: don't enter in the Konami Code while you're at Mr. Goofer's arcade or else you're not gonna like what happens next...

/ Sorry Linux users, but I've tried exporting to Ubuntu many times and for whatever reason (nerdy explanation here 🤓), GameMaker isn't connecting to the IP of my VBox virtual machine device. I already went through the official YoYo documentation, put the network as bridged adapter, gave the VM enough processers and RAM, and downloaded all of the Ubuntu commands required for it in terminal... but it's not wanting to work :/ I was so close to being able to compile it on Linux so I'm sorry. Hopefully eventually I can figure it out, because I want the game to eventually be playable on SteamDeck.

P.S. About a month or so ago, I cut the price of the game in half (from $12 to like $6), because honestly I'd rather give more people a chance to play the game and I already massively fucked up the ROI for the game anyway so you can enjoy it now for cheaper (for the few that actually did buy the game for $12 right when it came out, tysm for supporting me, I still very much appreciate that!) (Although money is a touchy subject, and I know there's still some ppl who probably think $6 is still too high... but that's literally the same amount as a cup of coffee or 1 crunchwrap supreme from taco bell ok give me a break) Also it's the Steam Summer Sale right now too so it's even cheaper, yipee!

P.S.P.S. If you're not already aware of "Stop Killing Games", and you live in the UK or EU, please sign the petition if you can! I'm not really sure why/if this is a controversial topic, but I do believe that if you purchase a game you should have the right to play it forever (I'm pretty sure indie devs are much more likely to hold this belief than AAA studios, lol). As long as Valve's servers are still up and running, Mr. Goofer's Mini Game Arcade Party will always be playable (majority of the game is essentially offline anyway, besides the leaderboards) but yeah.

thank you for listening to my ramblings, have a nice day! <3

notes.title: v1.1 (April 20) HAPPY EASTER! Easter Update
notes.content:
v1.10 (April 20th) 20 April (Happy Easter everyone!)

Version 1.1! From this point forward I'm not really sure if I should make a mini-announcement every single time I make a small tweak to the game, because it would probably clog up the game's Steam community tab... idk lol. 
- The manual is actually out now! Sorry that it wasn't available earlier but now it should be publicly viewable (still a work in progress, it'll improve as time goes on)
- Made secret achievement extra special when you hit the grand jackpot in Slots/Joker Poker
- Improved translations
- Linux version? yeah i know i still gotta do this... but idk man it'll come out eventually
- If you're reading this, please give this update post a THUMBS UP! (if you're cool!)
- You can now send a letter to Mr. Goofer in-game...

Okay... NOW is when I'd actually consider the game to be "fully complete". I know I released version 1.0 of the game back on Groundhog's Day, but... right now is when I'd actually consider the game to be a 100% finished work of art. 
Maybe I should've delayed the game? Yeah... I absolutely should have... I was an idiot. Now people's playthroughs of the game on YouTube and stuff are outdated... idk man. I learned a lot though.

but... OK! It's finally time to move onto other stuff! I have some exciting ideas and potential future projects planned... stay tuned! But honestly life has been a bit hard for me personally lately, so I'm not sure when these things will happen... but they'll happen eventually.

In the meantime, happy Easter! ːsteamhappyː

notes.title: v1.09 (April 11th)
notes.content:
v1.09 (11 April 2025)

* In case you didn't see the announcement earlier, the game's official SOUNDTRACK released on April 1st! (for APRIL FOOL'S DAY!) *

Jam out to plenty of retro tunes, please help support the game by buying it! Go get it now! https://store.steampowered.com/app/3477290

- Added all of the other languages to the game! (but auto-translated by computer so they're probably not 100% accurate...) I used "DeepL" translate which is more apparently accurate than Google is, and if the translation ends up not making any sense, I'm honestly not going to worry about it because this game is all supposed to be silly nonsense anyways xP
- The game's official manual is out NOW and will be continuously updated! It gives extra details, information, and lore about the game, plus other extra stuff!
- When balloons pop, the screen shakes! Also added even more silly sound effects!
- Goofball Pinball: Fixed an issue where it would immediately quit the Ski-ball game for no reason 
- Goofer Gambling, Inc. - In a normal game of blackjack, your cards have to add up to 21 without going over (a bust). I wanted to make "Stackjack" more unique, with more strategy to win the game, so now the number to get to is now randomly chosen between 11 and 41!
- Removed Gooferbrine

Next update will be version 1.1

notes.title: v1.08 - March 17th
notes.content:
v1.08 - 17 March (Happy St. Paddy's Day!)

- MENUS: Added a beautiful dotted border on the menu that switches colours back and forth! Tiny details like these add so much extra ~pizzaz~ and life to the game.
- Made some of the "MASTER" achievements less tedious to achieve
- Icebreaker: SUPER COOL new music!!!!!
- The Painful Platformer: fixed the door sound effect not playing when advancing to the next level
- Expert Exam: added a short delay before each option appears whenever you advance to the next question so that each option can be selected and shuffled without error

Okay, so here’s the deal with all of the other languages that the game was planning on supporting. Luckily I do know English (obviously), and also Swedish. But with all these 12 other languages (German, Dutch, Polish, Russian, Italian, French, Spanish, Portuguese, Simplified/Traditional Chinese, Japanese, Korean, etc etc...) This past week I was calculating how much each translation would cost, and it comes out to an estimate of like $200 per language? Not that my game is too text heavy to begin with. Now, I spent way too much money on this project and I am broke enough as it is. And unless there’s a website where people can translate your game for free, I don't see any of these languages being available in the game anytime soon.
UNTIL the other day when I had the idea that I could potentially just auto-translate the game with Google? And I can just put a warning on the screen saying that the translation was done by computer, so it’s not going to be 100% accurate (especially with CJK). Listen I know this method is cheap, but hey it’s better than nothing, right? 

ALSO- the game is currently 20% off for the Steam Spring Sale! 
The game's official manual, soundtrack, and Linux version are all still coming soon! After Version 1.10, I will be taking a break from updates for a while.

notes.title: v1.07 - March 11th
notes.content:
New Update! v1.07 - March 11th

- Updated the achievement icons! Also added two BRAND NEW secret achievements... 🤫
- Disco At Dusk: adjusted the press tolerance so that both early and late inputs for the arrows feel more balanced now (hopefully now it should feel better to play)
- When Pigs Can Fly: Added cute little honeybees that buzz around, along with a beautiful new rendition of the music!
- Odd Hue Out: apparently people thought this minigame was boring, so guess what?? I just added a fast timer to it so now you only have 5 SECONDS TO GET THE COLOR OR ELSE YOU LOSE!!!!!!!! How's that for a challenge huh?
- Recker: an off-duty cop that was supposed to be watching the prison inmates seems to have fallen asleep on the job... also, a collision issue that some people have encountered should now be fixed.
- Smiley Sticker Search: added film reel decoration onto the screen! now the mini game feels more like it's in a movie theatre.
- Mr. Goofer lost some weight on the title screen and looks less like a freaky animatronic (he's supposed to be an actual gopher)
- Config: Made links clickable! now the Svinta website actually pops up when you click on the contact link.
- Added the "right click" (B) input to the controls on the main menu (it wasn't listed before).

Stay tuned for the Soundtrack release, the Linux version, an official guide/manual for the game that will be coming out soon, and a bunch of other stuff!

notes.title: (2 March) v1.06
notes.content:
v1.06 (March 2)

- Redesigned the icons for ‘Goofball Pinball’ and ‘Coin Catch’ (it may take some getting used to, but I think they look a lot better)

- Also fixed up the look of a bunch of sprites, and added LOTS of new decorations here and there (for example, a dartboard in the pool room, a clown horn in the claw machine, an electric guitar and a toy drum as instruments in the disco room, and 80s decor such as a Rubik’s cube) small decorations/details like these really add life to the game

- Added a bunch of 8-bit sound effects throughout the game, to massively improve its atmosphere and make it really feel like you’re at a coin-op attraction

- Fixed a small issue that I didn't realize was happening until now (nothing too serious, just an oopsie lol) where the "coin insert" sound effect was still playing during a room transition, even when you're advancing to the next level within a minigame (it should now only play when entering a minigame)

- Pill Puzzle: added colorblind accessibility to the game, each pill type is now labeled with its own corresponding letter

- The Ball Pit Battle: added the “Punch-out” inspired sound effects (which is actually my voice lol)

- Expert Exam: revised the questions up a bit, and also further along into the game the four options now get randomly shuffled, so you actually have to read the question instead of relying on muscle memory (makes it more interesting and just a little bit harder, now you have to use your brain some more to think what the answer is!)
 
- Removed Gooferbrine

notes.title: v1.05 (16 February)
notes.content:
v1.05 (16 February)

- DUE TO POPULAR DEMAND... instead of unlocking each minigame one by one, now you unlock TWO AT A TIME!
So now, the game is less linear and you have the freedom to choose which of the two newly unlocked games that you want to play first. 

And if that other minigame is too hard or you don't want to reach its goal, you can just skip it and come back to it later.
(But in order to actually unlock the finale and beat the whole entire game, you still need to reach all of the 24 minigame goals, of course.)

[Personally I prefer doing all of the games back-to-back, since otherwise the game goes by rather quickly and you could kinda skip through the whole thing, but I suppose the customer/player is always right... so there you go!]
 
 - ALSO DUE TO POPULAR DEMAND: In the update previously, I lowered the goal point-requirement thresholds a bit so that each minigame is less long/fatiguing to complete, but some people have been saying that they're still too high... so now I just lowered them even more— AGAIN. 

Some examples: Reaching the goal for "Whack-A-Gopher" should take you no more than 1 minute now.  "Odd Hue Out"? Now that one takes half as long to complete, with a 50 pt. goal instead of 100. So now they're not as "stretched out". I suppose people really like their minigames to be rather "mini"...

- Added TWO BRAND NEW LEVELS to "A Gridlock Maze"! These new (optional) levels are larger, and need to be completed in order to get the master medal. I also adjusted the speed of dash mode, it's a bit slower to allow for more precise turns within the maze.

- Goofball Pinball: some people thought this game was WAY too hard, so I adjusted the gravity/physics of the pinball, now it moves around a lot more and goes a bit crazy. The physics system that the pinball uses is a bit hard to perfect, since there's a lot of tweaking and fine-tuning variables involved, but I tried the best I could to fix it up.

- Smarty Sort: one person said that sometimes the game wasn't registering whenever they click on a Smarty in order to drag it (?), especially when the Smartys start to move really quickly - so now, the Smartys move a bit slower whenever you're hovering over them with your mouse. So you should definitely be able to click 'em!

- ‘Icebreaker’: the snowball in the cube crush section now bounces around a lot more/is a bit faster

- 'Disco At Dusk' should be playable no matter what now, no more "oops, file error!". The game should also be working fine on Steam Deck, although I have to test it out to make sure (which is kinda hard for me because I don't have a Steam Deck (yet).

- Downer Diver, When Pigs Can Fly: now these up-n'-down games only have 4 lives instead of 5, since people said that they were way too easy.

- By default, the "ENABLE FILTER" option is now off. This is just in case a player's device cannot handle the maths behind the VHS/CRT shader graphics.

- Expert Exam: added four new questions!

- Trivial Timed Tasks: the toys in the "Gift Grabber" claw machine move around more wacky (wackily?) now! The flies in "Insect Issue" are also slower and give you less of a headache when they're buzzing around.

By the way.. thanks to all of those who have reviewed the game and written posts/articles and stuff about it! I really appreciate the positive reviews. :) Now, I do realize that less-than-positive reviews are inevitable... but whenever I hear any kind of criticism towards the game, I immediately go back and try my best to fix it.  So not only does the game get better, the bad review also then becomes obsolete! It's a win-win.

Especially for my first game though at 19yo, I think I did a pretty good job.  I mean, look at one of the best filmmakers of all time, Stanley Kubrick: his first movie only has a 5.3/10 review on IMDb... then his later works were literal masterpieces and he became the G.O.A.T. director! Point is... I learned a lot making this game, and it's getting better all the time. And I will try to make any potential future projects of mine a lot better. Anyways, thanks for reading this update and listening to my ramblings!

Linux support and the Soundtrack release will be coming up next!

notes.title: Hello players! + Linux version
notes.content:
Hello people! And to those who just found my game from Keymailer, welcome! I hope you enjoy my game :)

Release date is next week... the game is basically finished lol. but (of course) I am still going to continue to make minor adjustments, add polish, and make small tweaks and fixes if necessary. Right now I'm actually waiting on Valve to approve the release build of my game. Then, as soon as they do — Mr. Goofer's will be RELEASED! (woooo! ːsteamhappyː)

If you're from Keymailer: Hopefully your access keys work well! — earlier there was a bit of an issue where the wrong type of key was being sent out to people, but now that should all be fixed up and your product activation codes should be able to be redeemed and it should be working properly. I really hope you like Mr. Goofer's! And if you play the game, PLEASE! upload gameplay or a video about it to YouTube, that would really help out a ton!!! Like, seriously. I look forward to seeing any content that is made about it and I'll try to watch all of them! :)

* Another important note — I want to let everyone know that the Windows version of the game will only be available by the initial launch date of the game, BUT don't worry Linux users, as I am currently typing this out I am downloading a virtual machine and installing Ubuntu onto my computer so that I can compile my game so that it supports Linux! The whole thing is a bit of a technical complicated process, but it shouldn't take too long. The version for Ubuntu will be available as soon as possible.

Thanks again, and I'll see you all on Groundhog Day! (Will the gopher see his shadow? 🤔)

notes.title: Getting Ready by Groundhog Day... Release Update!
notes.content:
Hello everyone! I hope you all had a great holiday season. (A little late, I know we're already three weeks into January...)

Mr. Goofer's will be releasing on FEBRUARY 2nd! That's very soon! Too soon, even for me. 

IMPORTANT note: I want to be clear that the game will only be available in English (and maybe Swedish) when it releases. HOWEVER, I will constantly update the game whenever I add a new language. Having to pay a bunch of translators takes a bit of time! But they will get added eventually.

The game drops on Groundhog Day - obviously, I will keep updating it, adding small tweaks, fixing up any potential bugs (although I playtested the game many times and haven't found any), fixing it up a little bit here and there. The leaderboards will be up and running, they're a bit hard to test out but they should be in good shape by release.

 Although the game is a bit ridiculous, I spent a lot of time making it and I really hope you guys enjoy it. As a solo developer, I can't do a million things at once lol. The stress has been kind of getting to me. I also realized I'm going to be releasing my first commercial video game while I'm still technically a teenager, (my birthday is the week after release!) so that's funny. 

If you've had my game wishlisted for a while, or whether you literally just found my game and you're completely new here, thank you!

(Hey... does anyone even read these announcements?)

notes.title: Release Date Update… COMING SOON
notes.content:
Hello everyone! I’d like to thank you for your patience as I finish up the development of “Mr. Goofer’s Mini Game Arcade Party!” and prepare it for release.

I’m sure as you may know, the release date I set for the game was Q4 2024. And the end of the year is approaching… so here’s an update.

The game itself is pretty much 99% content complete! So if I really wanted to, I could just honestly release it like mid-December before the holidays… Unfortunately though, I really need more time for polish, translation, emails, and a bunch of other stuff that’s boring but necessary, so I’m going to have to delay the game a little bit into 2025. I really am just one person, a solo dev so I’d rather just take my time. That being said, right now the game is going to be in an “open beta” stage as I provide access keys to play testers, as well as press outlets so that they hopefully like my game enough to write articles about it. Contact me if you’re interested in getting the inside scoop.

“So, what’s the new release date for Mr. Goofer’s now?!” You may be asking (or not)

GROUNDHOG DAY 2025! (Er, Gopher Day 2025!)
That’s right, Feb 2. (Which is actually 9 days before my birthday 🥹)

That’s very early next year, so stay tuned!

For more information, read this thread (and for more dumb posts follow me on Twitter): https://x.com/KeriSvinta/status/1857268532922159384
